title: Second Novgorod Schra phase
summary: The selected Riga copy records 64 articles governing an oath-bound merchant community and later interaction with Diet regulation.
notes: 1295 is the dossier's selected documentary date; it is not a foundation date for the Kontor or Hanse.

title: Beginning of the regular general-diet record
summary: The evidence window preserves the difference between a modern synthesis dating regular Diets from 1356 and the surviving copied recess series beginning in 1361.
notes: A date range is used because the first Hansetag is disputed; no foundation event is asserted.

title: Temporary relocation from Bruges to Dordrecht
summary: Hanseatic merchants moved their Kontor from Bruges to Dordrecht for two years while negotiating commercial treatment.
notes: The event is a temporary institutional relocation and not a transfer of sovereignty.

title: Zuiderzee and IJssel towns enter the documented Diet record
actor: Harderwijk Elburg Kampen Deventer and associated towns
summary: Henn identifies 1367 as the first recorded Diet attendance for Harderwijk, Elburg, Kampen and Deventer in the study group.
notes: The row records attendance and does not label the towns as members.

title: Cologne Confederation conflict with Denmark
summary: A coalition overlapping only partly with the wider Hanse pursued conflict against Denmark before the Peace of Stralsund.
notes: The actor is named narrowly to avoid treating the confederation and the Hanse as identical.

title: Peace of Stralsund
summary: The treaty instruments dated 24 May 1370 record peace and renewed or expanded trading privileges.
notes: The familiar high-point interpretation remains qualified in the chronology ledger.

title: Ordinance forbidding trade with Flanders
summary: In May 1388 the Hanse left Flanders and forbade trade with Flemish merchants or goods that had passed through the county.
notes: The source documents widespread evasion; the row does not imply perfect enforcement.

title: Return of the Kontor to Bruges
summary: After compensation and renewed concessions, Hanseatic merchants returned from Dordrecht and re-established their Kontor in Bruges in December 1392.
notes: The return followed a negotiated settlement rather than a territorial acquisition.

title: Bruges building and House of Nations rights
summary: Charters granted exclusive building rights at Oosterlingenplein and access to a House of Nations.
notes: The privilege located merchants inside host-city law and does not constitute territorial sovereignty.

title: Bruges staple rights
summary: A charter confirmed staple rights for Hanseatic merchandise moving through Flanders and Brabant.
notes: No commodity volume is derived from the legal concession.

title: Bruges Rhenish wine excise reduction
summary: A concession reduced the excise payable on Rhenish wine handled by Hanseatic merchants.
notes: Third and last charter in the selected 1458-1502 Bruges group; the concession modifies a payment and does not confer territorial rights.

title: Suppression of Peterhof
actor: Ivan III, grand prince of Moscow
summary: The documentary dossier records the suppression of Peterhof in 1494.
notes: Closure of this establishment is not treated as dissolution of the wider Hanse. The actor is the Muscovite grand prince, not the Novgorod republic: Novgorod had been annexed by Moscow in 1478, so the host authority named in the 1295 Schra phase is not the authority that closed the establishment.

title: London Steelyard by-laws
target: Merchants represented through the London Kontor
summary: The by-laws regulated elections, internal jurisdiction, finances, conduct and training within the merchant community.
notes: Internal jurisdiction remained grounded in English host privileges.

title: Suppression of the London Kontor
summary: English authorities suppressed the Kontor in 1598, ending the selected late documentary phase.
notes: The event restricts a host-granted institution; it is not a wider Hanse dissolution.

title: Closure of the selected Steelyard phase
summary: The 1554 by-laws phase closes with suppression in 1598.
notes: A separate closure row supports event-type filtering while sharing the same documented act.

title: Last general Hanseatic Diet
summary: The 1669 assembly is the last general Diet in the reviewed chronology.
notes: The project records a conventional terminus and explicitly rejects the language of formal dissolution.

title: Bergen Kontor institutional afterlife
actor: Bergen merchant community and Lübeck custodians
summary: Bergen's court books continue to 1759, the last secretary left in 1761 and the archive transferred to Lübeck in 1764.
notes: The long afterlife demonstrates why 1669 is not a universal end date.
